content:
Leah: Heads-up: MediSys (Monica) sent a security questionnaire and a throughput ask. They want an enterprise commit for a clinical triage feature. Key perf ask: sustained 500 RPS during business hours, spikes to 900 RPS for ~10 min/day. Avg seq ~120, model family: long-context 2k (generation heavy). Need reserved GPUs proposal + burst policy and a plan for smoke test metrics for their execs.
Ryan: I can run the sizing. Quick Q: are embeddings separate infra or same endpoints? That affects reserved headroom.
Monica: embeddings on same service but routed to smaller model instances. Estimate tokens/day ~600M (includes embeds). Want 95p gen latency <350ms.
Oscar: For a 2k-context model at 120 tokens, throughput per A100-ish GPU ~300-450 RPS depending on batching and kv hits. For the 900 RPS spike I'd recommend baseline reserved 4 GPUs + 2 hot standby reserved for failover, plus burst credits to absorb spikes.
Ryan: Draft numbers (conservative/expected/aggressive):
- Conservative: reserved 4 GPUs, burst pool = 500M tokens/month, autoscale min=3, target_util=60%
- Expected: reserved 6 GPUs, burst pool = 1.2B tokens/month, autoscale min=4, target_util=70%
- Aggressive: reserved 8 GPUs, burst pool = 2B tokens/month, autoscale min=6, target_util=75%
Oscar: Add AZ spread (3 AZs preferred for regulatory workloads) and preheat windows before business hours: 15-30m. Also recommend a quantized fallback variant (8-bit) for spot/backfill.
Monica: Can you show the math so finance sees the assumptions? They want to know cost delta between reserved vs burst-heavy approach.
Ryan: Sure. Example calc for expected tier: spike tokens = 900 RPS * 120 tok * 600s/day * 30 days = 1.944B tokens (if they sustain 10min spikes daily). Baseline tokens = 500 RPS * 120 * (8h*3600s*20 business days) ~ 345.6M tokens. Total month ~2.29B tokens; reserved covers baseline compute and part of expected; burst credits cover spike delta. I'll convert to $ using current pricing tiers and include GPU-hour estimate for SOW.
Oscar: Ops runbook notes: prefill KV caches by replaying last 30m of production traffic during preheat; provide `kv-prefill --window 1800 --parallel 8` job in staging. Also use a health-check path pinned to fallback to keep it initialized.
Leah: Security/legal: MediSys needs KMS, VPC peering, subprocessor list, and 3yr audit log retention. @legal-bot can you confirm the contract language for audit retention?
legal-bot: Contract language for 3yr audit logs exists; I'll attach clause snippets. Need customer's SOC2 cert and DPA redlines.
Monica: We also need a live smoke test in PoC that proves 95p < 350ms. Can you run a test and capture p50/p95/p99, KV hit rate, GPU utilization, and token consumption?
Ryan: Plan: run three smoke tests in staging: 1) baseline 500 RPS for 30m, 2) spike 900 RPS for 10m inside a 30m run, 3) soak 300 RPS for 4 hours to validate steady-state. Example load command: 
```bash
rload run --target https://staging.redwood/medisys-gen \
  --profile long-context-2k --rps 900 --duration 600 --concurrency 300 \
  --seq 120 --metrics p50,p95,p99,gpu_util,kv_hit
```
Oscar: I'll monitor infra and provision temporary routing policy that prefers reserved pool and only evicts to fallback model when queue depth > 500.
Leah: Timeline: Ryan will deliver a short SOW appendix with three tiers + cost estimate by tomorrow EOD. Oscar will prepare the ops runbook snippets and preheat job today. Monica will upload sample traffic csv and send the security questionnaire. Legal-bot to share contract snippets.
Monica: Uploading traffic sample now. Also, can you include an example SLO note for the SOW (p95 < 350ms, availability 99.9% for reserved routes, burst best-effort)?
Ryan: Will include SLO language and a sample invoice break for reserved vs consumed burst.
Leah: One more ask: include fallback quality notes (we'll document expected ROUGE/bleu delta if using quantized fallback). Ops to run a few eval prompts against quantized variant during PoC.
Oscar: Will run evals and include quick diff chart.
Monica: This is great, timeline works for us. Thanks.
Leah: Thanks team :rocket:
